sentences.text: In Florida, winter cold fronts set the rhythm of offshore fishing.
Ahead of a front, winds blow from the south or southwest, the barometer falls, and clouds build.
As the front passes, a squall line can bring gusty winds and rain, and the wind shifts suddenly.
Behind it, the wind veers to the west, then northwest and north, often blowing hard for a day or two, while the barometer rises and the sky clears.
On the Atlantic side, those north winds blow against the Gulf Stream and make it dangerous.
The best fishing windows often come just before a front, or after the wind lies down behind it.
